newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nuevo Leon state sees citrus output up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nuevo Leon state sees citrus output up.

text.p: Citrus farmers from the northern state of Nuevo Leon expect to boost output in the 1997-1998 cycle by 50 percent over the predicted production for the closing 1996-1997 cycle.

"Our output this cycle was low, around 180,000 tonnes of fruit, although we should raise output in the upcoming cycle to 270,000, an increase of 50 percent," Gerardo Elizondo Barba, the chairman of Association of Regional Citrus Growers, told Reuters.
Nuevo Leon produces around 10 percent of the national citrus production estimated to have averaged 2.5 million tonnes of fruit in recent years.

Nuevo Leon's citrus production, mainly oranges, suffered a serious reverse in 1989 when a freeze hit plantations, damaging trees. But since then local growers have been building back up their harvest.

In the state, around 32,000 hectares are under production and a total of 6.4 million trees. Just 5,000 tonnes of mandarines were exported to Argentina, Canada and the United States from the output this cycle, Elizondo Barba said.
